properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the dev_storyflow field report (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27), 2026-09-23, the reporter's "Opportunity" after a false `undated` note: "on a revise, compute the note from the stored node after the merge."

WHY IT IS WIDER THAN ONE NOTE: the triage of 2026-09-28 found the same shape in three tools. The `undated` note reads `req.detected_at`; record_finding writes `unwrap_or` defaults into the merge; add_verification's guard reads `req.status`. All three read the CALL where the contract promises the stored node. See fact:root-cause-the-revise-contract-is-implemented-per-handler-and-guarded-by-instances-2026-09-28. The reporter asked about notes. The same question covers guards and defaults, and for guards it is not free.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(A) THE REPORTER'S, AS STATED — for reply notes only: compute the note from the node after the merge (for add_change_event, the `event` already in hand). Cheapest. It fixes the false alarm that "invites a needless re-send". A genuinely undated event still gets the note on every revise.
(B) WIDEN IT TO EVERY DERIVED BEHAVIOUR — notes, guards and defaults all read "passed, else stored, else default", through one merged view (for example, RequiredFields keeps and exposes the node it already fetches). This closes the class rather than the instance. It costs touching every handler with derived behaviour (four found today), and it changes what the add_verification guard means (see the counter-argument).
(C) SPLIT BY PURPOSE — notes and defaults read the merged node, but a guard whose job is to force a restatement stays on the call and NAMES the stored value in its refusal ("this check's last run is recorded as `passing`; re-send it with the findings"). Keeps the rule, removes the blind round trip.
(D) DOCUMENT, DON'T CHANGE — say in each description that a reply note reflects the call. Cheapest to build, and it contradicts the contract the same descriptions state ("omitted fields keep their stored value"). An agent reading the note still has to decide whether its date was lost.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: for notes and defaults, reading the merged node has no downside anyone has named. For GUARDS it has one. add_verification refuses findings without status because "a finding belongs to a RUN". If a revise's new findings describe a NEW run, inheriting the stored verdict pairs new evidence with an old verdict. That is the contradiction cap:a-check-records-what-it-found-separately-from-what-it-is already warns about (a check that recorded "EXIT 0, verdict STALE" and stayed passing forever). The call cannot tell a text correction of the last run's findings (the reporter's case) from a new run. That is why (C) exists. A second, smaller counter: under (A)/(B) an undated event gets the same note on every revise, which some would call nagging.

COST SHAPE, a finding and not a ranking: (A) is a one-line change in one handler. (C) is (A) plus one message. (B) is a shared mechanism plus four handlers plus the class-pinning test that the root-cause finding describes.
properties.name: OPEN — on a revise, should every reply note, refusal guard and default be computed from the node AFTER the merge rather than from the call — including a guard like add_verification's "findings need status", which exists to make a verdict be restated?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill as one question: whether revise-time computation reads the call or the merged node. The reporter's second idea from the same report ("keep omitted fields on record_finding revise") is NOT a separate Decision. It is exactly the fix for one measured defect, and it is recorded as that finding's proposed fix (fact:root-cause-record-finding-writes-its-defaults-on-every-revise-2026-09-28).

Near-matches read and judged NOT related: dec:idea-four-sibling-constructors-four-status-contracts (what status a CREATE lands in, superseded 2026-09-20; a different question). dec:idea-should-a-revising-write-say-what-it-removed (reporting a text shrink; its stated mitigation "a typed constructor merges, so passing only the field being changed leaves every other field untouched" is, as measured 2026-09-28, untrue for plan_epoch and record_finding, but that bears on that idea's premise, not on this question). dec:idea-should-a-large-node-be-changeable-one-field-at-a-time (the retype cost that produced the revise contract, not how derived behaviour reads it).
